sessionTitle: Deploy. Observe. Learn. Reinforcement learning for production agents

announcements.name: Developer tier training
announcements.shortDescription: A spot/low-priority SKU offering training at 50% off standard-tier cost, with the median supervised fine-tuning job costing about a dollar
announcements.longDescription: Developer tier (developer preview) is a training SKU selectable as a training type when starting a supervised fine-tuning run, allowing training at half the cost of a standard-tier job. It runs on a low-priority VM, so jobs may take longer, but it is well-suited for developers worried about fine-tuning being expensive. The training type options also govern data residency and cost.

announcements.name: Data zone SKU
announcements.shortDescription: Introduced at Build for residency guarantees in the US
announcements.longDescription: Introduced at Build [inferred] ("Adbuild" appears to be a mishearing of "at Build"), the data zone SKU is a training type that provides data residency guarantees in the US. It is offered alongside the developer preview and standard tier options when configuring a fine-tuning run.

announcements.name: Developer tier hosting
announcements.shortDescription: Hosting with no hosting fee to make experimentation cheaper
announcements.longDescription: Developer tier hosting is a newly introduced option with no hosting fee, making experimentation easy and cheap. It serves as a bridge to get fine-tuned models to production, after which substantial cost savings appear as usage ramps up. It complements developer tier training (spot capacity at 50% off), where the median supervised fine-tuning job costs about a dollar.

announcements.name: Fine-tuning skill for coding agents
announcements.shortDescription: A skill, available in GitHub Copilot for Azure or as a standalone download, that lets users describe fine-tuning goals in natural language and runs an autopilot flow that picks models, graders, and hyperparameters
announcements.longDescription: A newly added fine-tuning skill lets users employ their favorite coding agent and natural language to describe what they want to do, and the skill figures it out for them. In the demo, the presenter gave it the address of a hosted agent and described the goal (e.g., create a grader that checks the agent calls the right tools, gives partial credit, and reports how well the model performs), without having to learn the API or SDK or click around the UI. The demo used Claude and Copilot CLI [inferred] and was run ahead of time.
